mutmut 3.8.0 — re-running named mutants, and what a show diff looks like (phase 49 t6).
Scratch project: src/mod.py (functions b and msg), tests/test_mod.py, setup.cfg
  [mutmut] source_paths=src/ , pytest_add_cli_args_test_selection=tests/

$ mutmut run                                   (the full run: 13 mutants, 6 killed, 7 survived)
$ mutmut results --all true
  mod.x_b__mutmut_1: survived
  mod.x_b__mutmut_2: survived
  mod.x_b__mutmut_3: killed
  mod.x_b__mutmut_4: killed
  mod.x_b__mutmut_5: killed
  mod.x_b__mutmut_6: killed
  mod.x_msg__mutmut_1: survived
  mod.x_msg__mutmut_2: survived
  mod.x_msg__mutmut_3: survived
  mod.x_msg__mutmut_4: survived
  mod.x_msg__mutmut_5: survived
  mod.x_msg__mutmut_6: killed
  mod.x_msg__mutmut_7: killed

$ rm -rf mutants .mutmut-cache; mutmut run mod.x_b__mutmut_1 mod.x_msg__mutmut_5     (exact names, exit 0)
  progress line: "2/13  🎉 0 🫥 0  ⏰ 0  🤔 0  🙁 2" — exactly the two named mutants were tested
$ mutmut results --all true
  mod.x_b__mutmut_1: survived
  mod.x_b__mutmut_2: not checked
  mod.x_b__mutmut_3: not checked
  mod.x_b__mutmut_4: not checked
  mod.x_b__mutmut_5: not checked
  mod.x_b__mutmut_6: not checked
  mod.x_msg__mutmut_1: not checked
  mod.x_msg__mutmut_2: not checked
  mod.x_msg__mutmut_3: not checked
  mod.x_msg__mutmut_4: not checked
  mod.x_msg__mutmut_5: survived
  mod.x_msg__mutmut_6: not checked
  mod.x_msg__mutmut_7: not checked

With the previous results kept (no rm), the same command leaves every other mutant at its earlier status:
  (observed: results --all true still lists the earlier killed/survived statuses; the counter showed 13/13 from the cache,
   so only the cleared-cache run above proves that exactly the named mutants executed)

FINDING — `mutmut run <exact name>...` selects mutants by name; results --all true lists them with their status.
A mutant not run reads "not checked" when the cache was cleared, never "killed".

---- what `mutmut show` prints (the diff is relative to the FUNCTION; its def line is line 1) ----
$ mutmut show mod.x_b__mutmut_1
# mod.x_b__mutmut_1: survived
--- src/mod.py
+++ src/mod.py
@@ -1,4 +1,4 @@
 def b(x):
-    if x > 10:
+    if x >= 10:
         return x - 10
     return x * 2
$ mutmut show mod.x_msg__mutmut_1
# mod.x_msg__mutmut_1: survived
--- src/mod.py
+++ src/mod.py
@@ -1,4 +1,4 @@
 def msg(x):
-    if x < 0:
+    if x <= 0:
         raise ValueError("negative value")
     return "ok"
$ mutmut show mod.x_msg__mutmut_3
# mod.x_msg__mutmut_3: survived
--- src/mod.py
+++ src/mod.py
@@ -1,4 +1,4 @@
 def msg(x):
     if x < 0:
-        raise ValueError("negative value")
+        raise ValueError(None)
     return "ok"
$ mutmut show mod.x_msg__mutmut_5
# mod.x_msg__mutmut_5: survived
--- src/mod.py
+++ src/mod.py
@@ -1,4 +1,4 @@
 def msg(x):
     if x < 0:
-        raise ValueError("negative value")
+        raise ValueError("NEGATIVE VALUE")
     return "ok"
$ mutmut show mod.x_msg__mutmut_2
 def msg(x):
-    if x < 0:
+    if x < 1:
         raise ValueError("negative value")
     return "ok"
$ mutmut show mod.x_msg__mutmut_4
 def msg(x):
     if x < 0:
-        raise ValueError("negative value")
+        raise ValueError("XXnegative valueXX")
     return "ok"
$ mutmut show mod.x_msg__mutmut_6
 def msg(x):
     if x < 0:
         raise ValueError("negative value")
-    return "ok"
+    return "XXokXX"
$ mutmut show mod.x_msg__mutmut_7
 def msg(x):
     if x < 0:
         raise ValueError("negative value")
-    return "ok"
+    return "OK"

FINDING — a string mutant is either a literal replaced wholesale (`None`), wrapped (`"XXnegative valueXX"`),
or case-changed (`"NEGATIVE VALUE"`, `"OK"`); an operator mutant changes a token (`>` -> `>=`, `0` -> `1`).
A text-only change is therefore detectable by text alone: the lines differ only INSIDE a string literal
(`"XXokXX"`, `"OK"`), but `ValueError(None)` replaces the literal by code and is NOT text-only.
